Add Instrument value class and JSON adapter
commitResults.messageBody:
Members need to record each instrument they play together with the
number of years played, so that coordinators can later filter by
instrument and experience.

Instrument stores a trimmed name and a whole number of years (0-99).
Names are compared ignoring case and extra whitespace, so 'French Horn'
and 'french  horn' refer to the same instrument.

JsonAdaptedInstrument stores an instrument as {"name", "years"} so
the data file stays easy to edit by hand.

Neither class is used by Person yet; that follows in v1.3.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject decimal years when loading instruments from JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
Jackson truncated decimal years before validation, so a hand-edited
"years": 3.9 loaded as 3 and -0.5 loaded as 0. Values too large for an
int also wrapped around into the valid range.

Read years as a Number and accept only whole numbers that fit in an int.
Branch/61 partial name matching

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace tags with instruments across HiveMind
commitResults.messageBody:
Members are described by the instruments they play and for how long,
but tags could only hold free-form labels, so coordinators could not
record or filter by instrument.

Let's replace Tag with Instrument throughout:

* Person stores a set of instruments and rejects two instruments with
  the same name, ignoring case and spacing.
* add and edit accept i/INSTRUMENT:YEARS; edit keeps instruments when
  i/ is not given, replaces them when it is, and clears them on a
  bare i/.
* JSON storage saves instruments as name/years objects and rejects
  duplicate instrument names.
* filter matches whole instrument names with i/INSTRUMENT, replacing
  the temporary tag criterion until #68 adds status and minimum years.
* PersonCard, messages, sample data, test helpers, JSON fixtures, tests
  and the User Guide are updated to match.

The t/ prefix, Tag and JsonAdaptedTag are removed.

Closes #69.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject repeated instruments when loading JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
add rejects i/Violin:4 i/violin:4, but a data file with the same pair
loaded fine, because equal instruments collapsed into one when the
list was copied into a set before the duplicate check.

Let's check the loaded list itself for repeated names, so storage
enforces the same rule as the parser.

filter only tokenized i/, so input like "filter i/Violin s/member"
read "Violin s/member" as one instrument name and silently listed no
one.

Let's also tokenize the other field prefixes and reject them with the
usage message, as other unsupported input is. #68 can lift this for
s/ when it adds status filtering.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show Status and MemberType as enumerations
commitResults.messageBody:
The model class diagram draws Status and MemberType as plain classes,
but both are Java enums.

Let's mark them with the <<enumeration>> stereotype, as UML expects.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy instrument duplicate and null checks
commitResults.messageBody:
Instrument#hasDuplicateNames relies on a side effect inside a stream
predicate, which is easy to misread. parseInstrumentsForEdit asserts
its argument is non-null, leaving a branch that never runs while tests
have assertions enabled.

Let's use a plain loop for the duplicate check, and requireNonNull as
the rest of the parser does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Exclude UI code from Codecov coverage
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX UI classes need a display to run, which CI does not have, so no
automated test can cover them. Their lines still count towards Codecov
coverage, so any change to the UI lowers patch coverage.

Let's tell Codecov to ignore the ui package, as the course suggests for
code that is not normally covered by automated tests.

The Prefix class comment still uses the removed t/ prefix as its
example, and Extensions.css still defines an unused .tag-selector
style left over from AB3.

Let's switch the example to i/ and delete the unused style.
